A1.justification: Both PDFs describe IntroStyle, and their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison. The substantial synthetic-benchmark revision does not prevent matching the retained material.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval experiments on WikiArt, DomainNet, and SHacks, alongside parameter ablations and t-SNE analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original WikiArt and DomainNet results and reports ArtSplit evaluations, additional DomainNet ablations, and seed-dependent variability.

M1.justification: IntroStyle retains the same diffusion-feature extraction, channel-wise means and variances, diagonal Gaussian representation, and 2-Wasserstein distance. The default model, block index, and timestep remain unchanged. The synthetic-data redesign changes evaluation rather than the attribution algorithm.

E1.justification: SHacks is substantively replaced by ArtSplit: artist-name-free prompt-hacking detection becomes retrieval across crossed artistic styles and painting semantics. The represented artist population changes from 25 to 50, with 100 painting semantics. WikiArt and DomainNet coverage is retained.

E2.justification: The quantitative comparator sets in Tables 1 and 2 remain unchanged. However, v2 adds a supplementary WikiArt comparison against CSD in Figure 12, whereas v1's supplementary WikiArt retrieval grids showed IntroStyle alone. This is a limited expansion of comparative evaluation.

E3.justification: The synthetic evaluation changes from 25 queries each ranking 72 images to 100 queries each ranking 60,000 images. Table 2 replaces SHacks mAP@5/10 with separate Style-Eval@10 and Semantic-Eval@10 assessments using different positive labels. Prompt construction now explicitly includes artist names. The reported timestep sweep also expands from [25,950] to [0,950]; retained real-dataset splits and preprocessing are unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds separate semantic-bias diagnostics and fixed-semantic style-retrieval case studies on ArtSplit, plus DomainNet block-index and distance-metric ablations in supplementary Tables 6–7. It removes the WikiArt t-SNE clustering analysis and Jacob Jordaens subcluster case study from v1. The existing WikiArt parameter ablations remain.

E5.justification: Supplementary Section C in v2 newly reports seed-varying variances of 0.002 and 0.001 for mAP@10 and Recall@10 in the DomainNet discussion. v1 provides no corresponding uncertainty reporting. The number of runs, seed identities, and estimation details remain unspecified.

E6.justification: The synthetic results are replaced under different conditions: v1 reports IntroStyle SHacks mAP@5/10 of 0.823/0.793; v2 reports ArtSplit style/semantic scores of 0.823/0.114. In v2, DINO has the next-highest style score, 0.682, while GDA DINO has the next-lowest semantic score, 0.143. New DomainNet ablation results are added. Tables 1, 3, 4, and 5 retain their numerical values.

T1.justification: The diffusion equations, feature definitions, Gaussian-distance expression, and supplementary metric formulas in Equations 1–8 are retained. No new theorem, proof, or formal derivation is introduced; the new style/semantic scoring discussion concerns evaluation protocol.

C1.justification: The training-free attribution and superiority claims remain, but a central dataset contribution is redefined. The introduction replaces evaluation of indirect stylistic prompting with claimed comprehensive coverage of style–semantics combinations for assessing disentanglement. This changes the contribution's scope beyond renaming SHacks to ArtSplit.

C2.justification: v2 shifts the synthetic-results interpretation from detecting hacked prompts to measuring semantic bias and style selectivity, introducing 0.01 as the expected semantic score for an agnostic representation. It removes the t-SNE interpretation of within-artist stylistic diversity. The existing memory limitation and restriction to Stable Diffusion v2.1 remain.

D1.justification: The benchmark-generation recipe is substantially revised, including the artist list, crossed prompt combinations, explicit artist-name inclusion, and new system/user templates with 25-word limits in supplementary Section D. Core extraction hardware and preprocessing remain unchanged. The front-page access pointer changes from a code repository to a project website, while both appendices still promise future code and dataset release.

R1.justification: Dataset inspiration shifts from Prompting4debugging to CSD, with new citations on CLIP bias and diffusion representations. Prompting4debugging, Ring-a-bell, Hard Prompts Made Easy, and the embedding citation are removed. The principal positioning against externally trained attribution models remains. CSD's updated title and publication information refer to the retained comparator.

P1.justification: The abstract and benchmark-related narrative are rewritten, terminology changes, a Model Size subsection is introduced, and appendix sections are reorganized. Most method and related-work prose, together with the main section sequence, remains substantially intact.

P2.justification: v2 combines the method diagrams into a redrawn Figure 2, replaces hacked/innocent illustrations with a style-by-semantics grid, adds separate retrieval displays and DomainNet tables, and removes the t-SNE figures. Plots are restyled and supplementary comparisons expanded. The earlier supplementary WikiArt grids are retained as Figures 13–14 rather than newly added.

improvement.justification: ArtSplit's crossed design and added DomainNet ablations provide useful diagnostic evidence, but they accompany removal of SHacks and the t-SNE analysis. The new weighted evaluation scores are incompletely specified, and Figure 10's purported style prompt includes semantic content such as 'night sky.' New reporting also contains discrepancies: Table 7 implies a 0.005 mAP@10 gain, while the text states 0.05. These tradeoffs prevent a confident judgment of the principal revision's net quality benefit.
